html:
Around 552 monks brought silkworm eggs in secret from Central Asia to Justinian in Constantinople, by Procopius's account hidden in hollow canes. From them the Byzantine Empire built its own silk industry.

Before this all raw silk came from China along the Silk Road, and Persia controlled the trade and set the price. Justinian had tried to buy silk through other routes without success. The monks are said to have come from a land called Serinda, perhaps Sogdia or somewhere near it. Raising silkworms in the empire took years to grow.

Silk became a pillar of the Byzantine economy and state. Imperial workshops wove the finest cloth, and the purple silks were reserved for the court. Emperors used silk to pay officials and as gifts to foreign rulers. The same story appears from the other side as silkworms smuggled to Byzantium.
sum: Around 552 monks brought silkworm eggs in secret from Central Asia to Justinian in Constantinople, by Procopius's account hidden in hollow canes. From them the Byzantine Empire built its own silk industry.
